newsitem.title: USA: U.S. LPG market mixed following API data.
newsitem.headline: U.S. LPG market mixed following API data.

text.p: U.S. liquified petroleum gas (LPG) prices were mixed in quiet midday trade on Tuesday following the release of monthly inventory data and the near expiry of January material, players said.
The American Petroleum Institute monthly data showed a 2.8 million barrel build in total propane stocks in December to 43 million, 1.2 million barrels above year-ago levels.
Normal butane stocks, however, fared poorly, dropping 6.1 million barrels to 18.5 million barrels as of Dec. 31, 1996. Stocks are about 2 million below year-ago levels.
The report sharply pushed down propane values in the Midcontinent, where anytime January traded between 50.25 cents and 50.50 cents a gallon, 3.50 cents below Monday levels.
Spot Mont Belvieu, Texas, material edged down a quarter cent to 41.75/42.00 cents. February material traded at 41.50 cents.
"It's very quiet. A lot of people seem to have finished with January but nobody is quite ready to jump on February," said one Houston player.
Normal butane in Belvieu found some report following the API data, edging down about a half cent to 53.25/53.75 cents, traders said.

Meanwhile, the first cargo of LPG has been lifted from ELF Aquitaine's deep water offshore Nkossa field in the Congo. The facility is expected to have a total LPG output of more than 350,000 tonnes in 1997, rising to more than 500,000 tonnes in 1998, the company said. -- ((Laney Salisbury, New York Energy Desk +1 212 859 1631))
